name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Lifecycle: /spec:genesis (greenfield) → roadmap briefs → /spec:sketch → /spec:plan → /spec:run (design when due, then build, then review, each driver-stepped with one fresh-context reviewer and a derived verdict) → /spec:release; plus /spec:atlas, /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.166.0 — A whole-product note now blocks the final sign-off instead of every journey. A journey's approve control counts only the questions and notes raised on that journey's own screens, so a product-wide doubt no longer makes every journey unapprovable; when a journey is clean while product-wide notes remain, the review page says how many still block sign-off, and `--mark approved` refuses by name until they are answered. Recorded as ADR-0019. 7.165.0 — The journey review page answers to a design: design/chrome-mocks/review.html is the binding reference artifact, cited as design_source. The rail's Whole project count is derived server-side instead of looked up in a map that could never hold it, so the first paint, a ?clean render and a capture all carry the number the browser re-derives. The scope band states its scope as real DOM text rather than CSS generated content, five .rv-* utilities win back the cascade from the generic .rv button rule, and the composer's dead scope toggle is deleted. Tests pin the page again, this time opt-in so they outlive the spec's close. 7.164.0 — red-check's per-file legs quote the test path with single quotes, so a host whose test filenames carry a route parameter (TanStack file routes) no longer has bash expand the segment away and report every passing sanctioned pin as a hard broken-pin; the deviations close refusal now leads with the entry grammar itself — a line is well-formed only as a blank, a heading, a bullet, or an indented continuation of a bullet still open — so a session repairing the sidecar no longer rediscovers the rule by repeated failed marks.
